assignment.title: Algebra II Honors — Lesson 2 Day 2: Transformations of Parent Functions

optionRationales.absolute value: |x| is the absolute value function, with its V shape.
optionRationales.quadratic: Quadratic is x², a U-shaped curve; |x| makes a V with straight sides.
optionRationales.square root: Square root is √x, which starts at the origin and curves to the right only.
optionRationales.reciprocal: Reciprocal is 1/x, which breaks at x = 0; |x| is defined everywhere.

optionRationales.(0, 0): |x| is 0 at x = 0, its lowest value, so the V turns at the origin.
optionRationales.(1, 0): (1, 0) would be the vertex of |x − 1|; the parent function is not shifted.
optionRationales.(0, 1): (0, 1) would be the vertex of |x| + 1; the parent function is not shifted.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The graph of f(x) = |x| is shaped like…

solutionReview.headline: Read each attribute from the function itself: the rule it applies to x, and where its graph turns.
reasoning: Family: |x| takes the absolute value of x, and its graph is a V made of two straight rays, so its family is absolute value.
Vertex: |x| is never negative, and |0| = 0, so its lowest point, where the V turns, is (0, 0).

optionRationales.[0, ∞): A real square root needs a number that is not negative, and √0 = 0 is defined, so x starts at 0.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): Negative numbers have no real square root, so not every x is allowed.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): x = 0 works, since √0 = 0, so 0 belongs in the domain.

optionRationales.[0, ∞): √x gives the root that is not negative, starting at √0 = 0, so the outputs are 0 and up.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): √x always gives the root that is not negative, so outputs below 0 never appear.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): The output 0 happens at x = 0, so it belongs in the range.

optionRationales.(0, 1): At x = 0, 2⁰ = 1, so the graph crosses the y-axis at (0, 1).
optionRationales.(1, 0): A y-intercept has x = 0; this point has x = 1.
optionRationales.(0, 2): This uses the base, 2, as the output; at x = 0 the power is 2⁰.

optionRationales.y=0: As x goes left, 2ˣ shrinks toward 0 but never reaches it.
optionRationales.x=0: x = 0 is a vertical line, and 2ˣ is defined there; the question asks for a horizontal one.
optionRationales.y=1: y = 1 is a height the graph reaches, at (0, 1); an asymptote is a value it only approaches.

questions.prompt: Read the transformed absolute-value graph and determine the values of a, h, and k.
Describe every vertical reflection, vertical scale, horizontal translation, and vertical translation in the transformed square-root graph.
Map the parent-function point (1, 1) through the cubic transformation y = 2(x − 1)³ − 1.
Adjust a, h, and k until your exponential graph matches the target transformation.
Use the model g(x)=A·f(B(x−C))+D. Describe g(x)=f(x+3).

optionRationales.left 3: x + 3 = x − (−3), so C = −3 and the graph moves 3 units left.
optionRationales.right 3: This reads the sign inside f at face value; a change inside f works opposite to its sign.
optionRationales.none: The +3 is inside f with x, so the graph does move sideways.

optionRationales.up 3: The +3 is inside f, with x, so it moves the graph sideways, not up.
optionRationales.down 3: The +3 is inside f, with x, so it changes the horizontal position, not the vertical one.
optionRationales.none: Nothing is added outside f, so D = 0 and there is no vertical move.

optionRationales.horizontal compression: With x multiplied by 2 inside f, each output is reached at half the x-value: the graph squeezes toward the y-axis.
optionRationales.horizontal stretch: This reads the factor inside f at face value; a factor inside f, with x, works in reverse.
optionRationales.vertical stretch: A vertical stretch multiplies the output, as in 2f(x); here the 2 multiplies x inside f.

optionRationales.2: This uses B itself, but a factor inside f works in reverse.
optionRationales.1/2: With B = 2, the horizontal scale factor is 1/B = 1/2.
optionRationales.−2: A negative factor would also reflect the graph; f(2x) has no negative, and a factor inside f works in reverse.

optionRationales.across the y-axis: The negative is inside f, with x, so each point (x, y) moves to (−x, y).
optionRationales.across the x-axis: An x-axis reflection is −f(x), a negative on the output; this negative is on the input.
optionRationales.across y=x: Reflecting across y = x swaps x and y, which makes an inverse; f(−x) only changes the sign of x.

optionRationales.none: Nothing is added to x or to f(x), so the graph does not slide.
optionRationales.right 1: −x is a reflection, not a shift: nothing is subtracted from x.
optionRationales.left 1: −x is a reflection, not a shift: nothing is added to x.

optionRationales.across the x-axis: The negative in −2 is in front of f, so every output changes sign.
optionRationales.across the y-axis: A y-axis reflection needs a negative inside f, with x; this negative is in front of f.
optionRationales.none: The factor in front of f is −2, and its negative sign is a reflection.

optionRationales.stretch by 2: |A| = 2 multiplies every output, so the graph stretches vertically by 2.
optionRationales.compression by 1/2: This treats a factor outside f like one inside; only a factor inside f, with x, works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The 2 in −2 multiplies every output, so the height does change.

optionRationales.right 1: x − 1 means C = 1, so the graph moves 1 unit right.
optionRationales.left 1: This reads the sign inside f at face value; a change inside f works opposite to its sign.
optionRationales.none: The −1 is inside f with x, so the graph does move sideways.

optionRationales.up 3: D = 3 is added outside f, so every point moves up 3.
optionRationales.down 3: This reverses a change made outside f; only changes inside f, with x, work opposite to their sign.
optionRationales.none: The +3 is added after f, so the graph does move vertically.

questions.prompt: Read the transformed cube-root graph and determine a, h, and k.

optionRationales.none: The factor inside f is a positive 3, so inputs keep their signs: no horizontal reflection.
optionRationales.across the y-axis: A y-axis reflection needs a negative inside f; the negative here is in front of f.
optionRationales.across the x-axis: A flip across the x-axis is vertical; a horizontal reflection comes only from a negative inside f.
The negative in front of f changes the sign of every output.
optionRationales.across the y-axis: A y-axis reflection needs a negative inside f, with x; this negative is in front of f.
optionRationales.none: The minus sign in front of f multiplies every output by −1, which is a reflection.

optionRationales.compression by 1/3: B = 3 inside f squeezes the graph toward the y-axis by a factor of 1/3.
optionRationales.stretch by 3: This reads the factor inside f at face value; a factor inside f, with x, works in reverse.
optionRationales.unchanged: The 3 multiplies (x + 2) inside f, so the width does change.

optionRationales.left 2: x + 2 = x − (−2), so C = −2 and the graph moves 2 units left.
optionRationales.right 2: This reads the sign inside f at face value; a change inside f works opposite to its sign.
optionRationales.none: The +2 is inside f with x, so the graph does move sideways.

optionRationales.up 4: D = 4 is added outside f, so every point moves up 4.
